_comment: Owner: contract-architect. Machine-readable expectations for every file in
this directory. Files whose name starts with an underscore are metadata and
DefinitionValidationError, and every code listed in
stage=registry   -> validate_definition() must SUCCEED (the document is
structurally fine) and the named error must be raised by
the query compiler / registry stage, i.e. by
registry. That split is the whole point of ADR 0001
section 4: structure and field resolution are two

malformed_field_key.json.note: Key grammar: no spaces, no punctuation, must have a namespace, must not be empty.

smuggled_orm_path.json.note: The attack this contract is built against: a double underscore in a key and an extra 'orm_path' member on a column. Both are rejected before anything reaches the ORM.

unknown_operator.json.note: 'regex' is not in the Operator enum. Operators are a closed set.

wrong_schema_version.json.note: Refuse to guess what a future document means.

filter_value_type_mismatch.json.note: relative_last_days needs a whole number of days, not a string. This is as far as type checking gets without a registry.

filter_value_wrong_shape.json.note: between wants exactly two values, in wants a non-empty list, is_empty wants no value at all.

filters_too_deep.json.note: Exactly one level of nesting (SPEC.md F6).

duplicate_sorting.json.note: The second stage on the same field can never have an effect.

unknown_top_level_key.json.note: Strict allow-list at every level, including inside 'options'. Unknown members are rejected, never ignored.

empty_columns.json.note: A report without columns can only ever produce an empty export.

unknown_aggregate.json.note: 'median' is not in the Aggregate enum.

ambiguous_filter_node.json.note: A filter node is a group or a condition, never both and never neither.

unknown_field_key.json.note: Structurally impeccable keys that simply do not exist. 'answer.question-that-was-renamed' is the realistic case: Question.identifier can be changed by the user at any time (docs/pretix-api-notes.md section 6.4).

field_type_conflict.json.note: 'contains' on a money field. Only the registry knows order.total is money, so this cannot be caught structurally.

sort_not_sortable.json.note: Sorting by an aggregated value is out of scope for v1; the registry marks position.price as not sortable on base 'order'.

missing_aggregate_on_order.json.note: Position-level fields on an order-based report must carry an aggregate (SPEC.md F3, ADR 0001 section 7).
